mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profits, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in less than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and an increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint movement of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not produce positive 20d returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (defined by housing starts above 1500 thousand units and GDP growth above 2.0% year-over-year), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to profit-taking and rising interest rates, leading to negative returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in less than 45% of late-cycle expansion periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The correlation between INDPRO and 20d SPX returns is less than 0.05 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5%, it signals accelerating inflation that may prompt the Fed to tighten policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in less than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer and housing demand, which boosts economic growth and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in RSAFS and HOUST does not result in positive 20d returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), the labor market is tight, leading to wage pressures and potential inflation, which causes the Fed to tighten, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in less than 45% of low-unemployment regime periods.
